# The Brief - NZ Politics Without The Spin

## Overview
The Brief is an independent, reader-funded political news source for New Zealand. We provide clear explainers on bills, budgets, and elections — no jargon, no bias, just facts. Our mission is to help New Zealanders understand what Parliament is actually doing so they can vote with confidence and hold power to account.

## Key Pages

### Main Navigation
- **/** - Homepage with latest explainers, newsletter signup, and featured content
- **/explainer** - Browse all political explainers by category (Politics, Technology, Business, Science, Health, Culture)
- **/quiz** - VoteFinder: 20-question quiz to match your values with NZ political parties for the 2026 election
- **/mp-lookup** - Find your Member of Parliament by address or postcode
- **/about** - About The Brief: our mission, methodology, and team
- **/methodology** - How we research, write, and fact-check every explainer
- **/contact** - Contact form for feedback, corrections, and topic suggestions

### Newsletter
- **/newsletter/confirmed** - Email subscription confirmation page
- **/newsletter/unsubscribed** - Email unsubscription confirmation page
- **/newsletter/error** - Newsletter error handling page

## Content Categories

### Politics & Parliament
Explainers covering New Zealand government, electoral systems, and parliamentary processes:
- How MMP (Mixed Member Proportional) voting works
- The role of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
- How bills become law
- Question Time and parliamentary procedure

### Policy Areas
- Housing affordability and property market policies
- Climate change and environmental legislation
- Healthcare and PHARMAC funding
- Education policy and funding
- Taxation and government spending
- Immigration and border policies
- Law and order, policing, and justice
- Workers' rights and employment law

### 2026 Election Resources
- **VoteFinder Quiz** (`/quiz`) - Interactive tool matching voters to parties based on 25 values-based questions covering:
  - Housing affordability vs. property investor interests
  - Climate action vs. industry impact
  - Tax policy and public services
  - Co-governance and Māori rights
  - Immigration levels
  - Healthcare privatisation
  - Benefit levels and social welfare
  - Law and order approaches
  - Education funding models
  - Foreign investment restrictions
  - Treaty of Waitangi principles
  - Defence spending
  - Three Waters policy
  - Smoking regulations
  - Superannuation age

## API Endpoints for AI Consumption

### Content APIs
- **/api/content/explainers** - JSON array of all explainers with title, summary, category, slug, and reading time
- **/api/content/parties** - Summary of NZ political party positions on key issues
- **/sitemap.xml** - XML sitemap with all pages and their priorities

### Newsletter APIs
- **/api/newsletter/signup** - POST endpoint for email subscriptions
- **/api/newsletter/confirm** - GET endpoint for subscription confirmation
- **/api/newsletter/unsubscribe** - GET endpoint for unsubscription

### Open Graph
- **/api/og** - Dynamic Open Graph image generation for social sharing

## Site Structure for LLMs

### Primary Content Type: Explainers
Each explainer follows this structure:
- **Title** - Clear, descriptive headline
- **Summary** - 1-2 sentence executive summary (visible in listings)
- **Category** - Organized by topic area
- **Reading Time** - Estimated time to read (typically 4-7 minutes)
- **Published Date** - When the explainer was published
- **Key Points** - "The essentials" bullet list for quick scanning
- **Article Body** - Full explainer content in plain English
- **Share Links** - Social sharing buttons

### Schema Markup Implemented
- **WebSite** - Homepage structured data
- **Organization** - Publisher information with logo
- **Article** - Individual explainer pages with headline, description, dates, author
- **BreadcrumbList** - Navigation breadcrumbs on all pages
- **FAQPage** - Quiz and methodology pages with Q&A structure
- **SearchAction** - Site search potential action

## Content Quality Standards

### Writing Principles
1. **Plain English** - No jargon without explanation
2. **Three Questions** - Every explainer answers: What is this? Why does it matter? What happens next?
3. **Source Transparency** - Primary sources cited (Hansard, legislation, official statistics)
4. **Non-partisan** - No party endorsement; balanced analysis
5. **5-Minute Read** - All explainers designed for quick consumption

### Fact-Checking Process
1. Topic selection based on public interest
2. Research from primary sources (bills, parliamentary records)
3. Plain English writing
4. Independent fact-checking
5. Editorial review for balance and clarity
6. Corrections policy with transparency

### MPs and Electorates

- Next.js 14+ with App Router

## Accessibility
- Semantic HTML5 structure
- ARIA labels where appropriate
- Keyboard navigation support
- Alt text for images
- WCAG 2.1 AA compliant design
- Text-first design - content readable without CSS
